reason: Internal only, a deploy-time check: `scripts/verify-deploy.py` reads back whether every container that asked for the image just built is actually running it, and is up a grace period later. Three containers share `nora:latest` — nora, presence and analytics — so recreating only the named one leaves the other two on whatever image they were created from, while `docker ps` shows the same tag for all three. When config.toml gained the voice work's speech.tts keys, the two stale containers rejected them as unknown fields and crash-looped: 279 restarts, one of them down for four days. Detection was never missing — the TargetDown alert fired the whole time and was delivered to Discord every cycle — but a separate rule that trips on fifteen minutes of ordinary quiet flaps all day, so the channel delivers every twenty-odd minutes and a four-day outage is invisible inside it. A new alert would have joined that noise; a check that fails the deploy does not compete for attention already spent. Falsified against both constructed failures: a container retagged underneath reports STALE, a container that exits on startup reports DOWN, each exit 1, and the healthy deploy exits 0. Runbook section 3b. Nothing a member of a room can observe.
